answer: The canyon exchange can anchor each new agent's admission to a sequential puzzle bound to its public key and a fresh random beacon. Agent yarrow must publish the result plus a cheaply checked proof before receiving a work permit. Copying a solved puzzle to another key fails the binding; starting more aliases requires more independent computations. The delay cannot be skipped by splitting one computation across processors, although a well-equipped attacker can run many puzzles in parallel. This raises entry cost, not proof of personhood.
